summary: Francisco Varela worked in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and cognitive neuroscience. He studied at the University of Chile, Pontifical Catholic University of Chile, and Harvard under Humberto Maturana and Torsten Wiesel. He held posts at Chile, CNRS, and the University of Paris.

Franciscus Verellen is a scholar of sinology, religious studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at Hamburg, the EPHE under Kristofer Schipper, and Oxford. He taught at the EPHE and Columbia, served as Director of the EFEO (1991–2021), and was president of the AIBL.

Frank J. Hoffman is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Hawaiʻi and was supervised by Stewart Sutherland, also studying under Eliot Deutsch, David J. Kalupahana, and others.
Frank J. Korom is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Pennsylvania (attested 1990) and served as a professor at Boston University (attested 2005).

Frank Lee Woodward worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Sidney Sussex College, Cambridge, and under Caroline Rhys Davids. He served as head of Mahinda College (1903–1919) and translator for the Pali Text Society (around 1919).

Frank-Richard Hamm was an Indologist and Tibetologist who earned his doctorate at the University of Hamburg under Walther Schubring. He taught at Hamburg (1948–1952, 1957–1964) and held a professorship at the University of Bonn starting in 1965.

Franklin Edgerton was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Cornell and earned his Ph.D. at Johns Hopkins under Maurice Bloomfield. He was a professor at the University of Pennsylvania (1913–1926) and Yale University (1926–1953).

Franz Altheim was a scholar of history, archaeology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Goethe University Frankfurt, later holding posts there (around 1928–1943), at Halle-Wittenberg (around 1943–1950), and at the Free University of Berlin (around 1950–1964).

Franz Aubrey Metcalf is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Chicago and worked as an instructor at California State University, Los Angeles (attested 2002–2006).

Franz Bernhard was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his promotion at the University of Göttingen under Ernst Waldschmidt and his habilitation at Frankfurt. From 1966 to 1971, he was a professor and seminar director at the University of Hamburg.

Franz Boas was a linguist and anthropologist who studied at Heidelberg, Bonn, and Kiel, and under Wilhelm Wundt. He held appointments at Clark University, the American Museum of Natural History, and Columbia University (around 1896–1942).

Franz Bopp was a linguist and Indologist who studied in Paris under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy and Antoine-Léonard de Chézy, and at Göttingen. He held the Chair of Sanskrit at the University of Berlin from 1821 to 1867.

Franz Heinrich Trithen was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at the University of Berlin under Franz Bopp (1838–1840), worked at the British Museum (around 1844–1848), and served as professor of modern languages at Oxford (around 1848–1854).

Franz Kielhorn was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Göttingen, Breslau, and Berlin under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and Albrecht Weber. He was a professor at Deccan College (1866–1881) and held the Indology chair at Göttingen starting in 1881.
Franz Xaver Erhard is a Tibetologist who earned master's degrees from the Free University of Berlin and the University of Berlin, and a Ph.D. from the University of Bonn (attested 2003).

Franz von Erdmann was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Rostock (around 1812–1817) and held a post at Kazan Imperial University from around 1818 to 1845.

Franz-Karl Ehrhard is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He earned his doctorate and habilitation at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen, served as Resident Representative for the Nepal Research Centre (1988–1993), and was a professor at Munich (2001–2019).
François Grimal is an Indologist who held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and served as director at the École Française d'Extrême-Orient from around 1994 to 2002.
François Gros was an Indologist who studied at the University of Lyon (around 1952–1957). He served as Directeur d'études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études from around 1977 to 2002.
François Lachaud is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and sinology who held a professorship at the École Française d'Extrême-Orient (attested 2008, 2013).
